name: Compute (training)
description: Frontier training compute — H100/B200-class clusters at 100K+ accelerator scale used for foundation-model training runs.

tightness.note: Frontier training runs use 100K+ H100-equivalents; allocations contested across hyperscalers

trajectory.note: Frontier training compute growing ~4-10x/yr; supply ramp lags demand

timeToRelieve.note: New fab capacity 2-4 yr; new GPU generations on 1-2 yr cycle

geographicConcentration.note: Most frontier training compute in US data centers; UAE/Singapore growing

notes: The headline bottleneck. NVIDIA-led GPU supply, hyperscaler cluster build-out, and TSMC fab capacity are the three sub-constraints.

name: Compute (inference)
description: Serving capacity for deployed models — accelerator-hours per token across cloud and edge deployment.

tightness.note: Major releases regularly hit capacity limits; reasoning models multiply inference cost 10-100x

trajectory.note: Demand growth (reasoning chains, agents) outpacing efficiency gains and capacity adds

timeToRelieve.note: Inference is more parallelizable; custom silicon (Trainium, TPU, Groq) helping

costToExpand.note: Substantial but lower per-FLOP than training; commoditizing

geographicConcentration.note: Many regions, but US/EU dominant; latency forces geographic distribution

notes: Less single-point-of-failure than training. Inference is where most users feel capacity constraints (rate limits, queues).

name: Fab capacity
description: Leading-edge semiconductor fabrication (3nm and below) — the upstream constraint behind nearly all frontier AI accelerators.

tightness.note: TSMC sub-3nm sold out 12+ months ahead; one credible supplier for frontier nodes

trajectory.note: TSMC Arizona, Samsung Texas, Intel Foundry expanding; multi-year ramps

timeToRelieve.note: Fab buildout 3-5 yr; equipment lead times 1-2 yr

costToExpand.note: $20-40B per leading-edge fab; only 3 firms can plausibly attempt

geographicConcentration.note: TSMC Taiwan dominant; ASML EUV monopoly. Geopolitical concentration risk.

notes: The upstream chokepoint. US CHIPS Act and Taiwan tensions make this the bottleneck with the highest strategic salience.

name: HBM / memory supply
description: High-bandwidth memory (HBM3/HBM3E/HBM4) — paired with logic dies in every frontier accelerator. Memory bandwidth, not FLOPS, often gates throughput.

tightness.note: SK Hynix HBM3E sold out into 2026; memory bandwidth gates accelerator throughput

trajectory.note: Each chip generation increases HBM stack count; demand outpaces DRAM fab additions

timeToRelieve.note: DRAM fab lead times shorter than logic; HBM packaging (CoWoS) is the bottleneck within the bottleneck

costToExpand.note: Multi-billion DRAM and packaging capex; CoWoS capacity at TSMC is gating

geographicConcentration.note: South Korea dominant for HBM; Taiwan for advanced packaging

notes: Often overlooked. The reason H100 and B200 supply is constrained is as much HBM and CoWoS as logic-die wafers.

name: Energy / power
description: Grid interconnect capacity, generation, and transmission — increasingly the rate-limiter for new datacenter siting.

tightness.note: Multi-GW interconnects waitlisted 5-10 yr in major US grids; UK, Ireland, Netherlands at moratorium

trajectory.note: Gigawatt-scale clusters proposed; grid build-out 5-10x slower than datacenter demand

timeToRelieve.note: Transmission line permitting 5-10 yr; new generation (nuclear, gas) similar

costToExpand.note: Interconnect upgrades $100M-$1B per site; new generation in $B

geographicConcentration.note: Many viable regions globally, but per-site permitting is the constraint

notes: Replacing compute as the headline bottleneck for next-generation clusters. Stargate, Microsoft-Constellation, and Meta nuclear deals all reflect this.

name: Cooling / siting
description: Water rights, land, climate suitability, and zoning for hyperscale datacenters.

tightness.note: Water-cooled designs constrained in arid regions; direct-liquid cooling reduces water demand

trajectory.note: Air and direct-liquid cooling retrofits expanding; sites still available outside drought regions

timeToRelieve.note: Datacenter construction 1-2 yr once site and power are secured

costToExpand.note: Site acquisition and construction in $100M-$1B range

geographicConcentration.note: Many viable global sites; concentration follows power and fiber availability

notes: Less acute than power but interacts with it — water-cooled efficiency is what makes some 100MW+ sites viable.

name: High-quality training data
description: Pretraining corpora — text, code, multimodal data of sufficient quality to drive frontier model improvements.

tightness.note: Public web text approaching exhaustion at frontier scale; quality filtering aggressive

trajectory.note: Tightening for novel human-generated data; loosening via synthetic data and licensing deals

timeToRelieve.note: Synthetic generation pipelines, real-world telemetry, and licensed corpora maturing

costToExpand.note: Licensing deals (NYT, Reddit, Shutterstock) in $10s-$100s of millions; labeling at scale

geographicConcentration.note: Data sources are global; legal regimes (GDPR, copyright) regional

notes: Synthetic-data viability is the open question. If synthetic scales, this bottleneck loosens; if not, real-data licensing becomes a moat.

name: Evaluation data
description: Benchmarks, held-out test sets, and dangerous-capability evals used to measure frontier-model progress and safety.

tightness.note: Public benchmarks saturating; contamination widespread; few credible held-out evals

trajectory.note: Public benchmarks tightening (saturation); private holdout sets from AISIs and labs emerging

timeToRelieve.note: Eval suite development 6-18 months; held-out test creation iterative

costToExpand.note: Eval data cheap relative to training data; expert annotation is the cost driver

geographicConcentration.note: Eval development globally distributed; AISIs concentrated in US/UK/EU

notes: A governance-critical bottleneck. Bad evals → labs can't credibly self-report risk → safety commitments lose teeth.

name: Algorithmic insights
description: Research breakthroughs in architectures, training procedures, post-training methods, and reasoning techniques.

tightness.note: Key insights diffuse fast via papers, code, and lab transitions; some methods stay private 6-18 months

trajectory.note: Open-weight releases (DeepSeek, Llama, Mistral) and academic publications keep diffusion fast

timeToRelieve.note: Papers and code propagate in weeks once published

geographicConcentration.note: Research community is global; lab concentration in US/UK/China

notes: The least supply-constrained bottleneck. The question is whether closed labs can sustain a multi-month research lead.

name: Talent supply
description: Frontier ML researchers, alignment researchers, and senior engineering staff capable of operating at the capability frontier.

tightness.note: Top frontier-ML researchers ~1000s globally; alignment researchers ~100s; compensation reflects scarcity

trajectory.note: PhD pipelines growing, but slowly; lab hiring frenzy bids up the senior tier

timeToRelieve.note: PhD pipelines 5-10 yr; senior engineering experience harder to manufacture

costToExpand.note: Senior researcher comp packages reach $1M-$10M; aggressive cross-lab poaching

geographicConcentration.note: US Bay Area, UK, China dominate; visa policy is a material lever

notes: A slow-moving bottleneck. Less acute than compute today, but the long pipeline makes shocks (e.g. visa restrictions) hard to recover from.

name: Capital
description: Investment capital for frontier training runs, infrastructure buildout, and operating losses during scaling.

tightness.note: Frontier labs have access to $10s-$100s of billions; trailing labs more constrained

trajectory.note: Sovereign wealth (UAE, Saudi), hyperscaler commitments, Stargate-scale infrastructure deals

timeToRelieve.note: Capital can be deployed in months when investor appetite exists

costToExpand.note: Capital is fungible; the question is access, not creation

geographicConcentration.note: US capital markets dominant; sovereign-wealth tier is the swing player

notes: Capital is the least constrained input for top-3 labs. For everyone else it is the binding constraint.

name: Deployment infrastructure
description: APIs, enterprise integrations, agent frameworks, and tooling needed to put model capabilities in front of users.

tightness.note: Major API providers mature; enterprise integration and agent tooling still nascent

trajectory.note: API ecosystems, agent frameworks (MCP, agent SDKs), and enterprise pipelines maturing

timeToRelieve.note: Engineering effort scales with capital; not capacity-bound

costToExpand.note: Engineering cost, not capex; standard SaaS economics

controllers: Cloud platforms (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Vertex)

geographicConcentration.note: API access global where not legally restricted

notes: Less a supply bottleneck than a maturity bottleneck. Affects deployment timelines more than capability frontier.

name: Regulatory friction
description: Legal, regulatory, and compliance constraints — EU AI Act, US export controls, sectoral rules, liability frameworks.

tightness.note: EU AI Act and US export controls binding for some uses; not capability-gating for frontier training in the US

trajectory.note: EU enforcement ramping; US export controls expanding; California SB-53 and sectoral rules emerging

timeToRelieve.note: Legislative cycles slow; rule-making takes years

costToExpand.note: This is a constraint, not a resource to expand

geographicConcentration.note: Brussels Effect plus US-China bifurcation creating regional regulatory regimes

notes: The bottleneck most amenable to deliberate governance intervention. Tightening it (more rules) reduces risk but slows deployment; loosening it does the opposite.
